prompt:
A variant of merge sort combines its two sorted halves in Θ(n log n) time instead of Θ(n) (for example, by naively re-sorting the combined half with heapsort). What is the overall running time?

Here n is the number of input elements; other symbols are defined in this question’s formula cards. Big O is an asymptotic upper bound; Θ and Ω denote matching growth and a lower bound.

options.explanation: This would hold if the combine step were linear. Here each level does more than n work.

Correct. Every halving level adds another factor proportional to the logarithm of its subproblem size. Summing those shrinking logarithmic terms adds a second logarithmic factor, as the worked card derives.
The recurrence still halves subproblem sizes, giving logarithmically many levels rather than a quadratic degeneration.

options.text: Θ(n log n log log n)
options.explanation: The extra cost is one full logarithmic factor, rather than a logarithm of a logarithm. The recurrence derivation in the worked card distinguishes them.

workedExample:
Write the recurrence and sum the recursion tree level by level:

```formula
T(n) = 2 T(n / 2) + n log(n)
W_k = 2^k(n / 2^k) log(n / 2^k)
W_k = n(log(n) − k)
T(n) ≈ n(log(n) + … + 2 + 1)
T(n) ≈ n(log(n))^2 / 2
where
T(n): the running time of the variant on n elements
n: the number of elements
log n: the base-2 logarithm of n, which is also the number of levels
W_k: the total work on level k of the recursion tree
k: the level number, from 0 at the root to log n
2^k: the number of pieces on level k
n / 2^k: the size of each piece on level k
log: the base-2 logarithm
…: "and so on", counting down by 1
≈: approximately equal to
In words: each level costs n times a log that shrinks by 1 per level, and adding those up gives about n (log n)² / 2.
```

So the time bound is Θ(n (log n)²), for n input elements. This is the master theorem's case where the logarithmic-factor combine work, sits just above the n per level of a linear merge by a log factor. It shows why the *linear* merge is what makes merge sort optimal.
